sections.label: Pupil-Teacher Ratio improvements
sections.summary: Pupil-Teacher Ratio has improved over the last decade and is currently 15:1 for primary, 12:1 for secondary and 11:1 for junior colleges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Over the last decade, our Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) has improved and is currently 15:1 for primary schools, 12:1 for secondary schools and 11:1 for junior colleges.

sections.label: No broad-based class size reduction
sections.summary: For these reasons, no broad-based reduction in class sizes will be implemented.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Because of these reasons, we have decided not to implement any broad-based reduction in class sizes.

sections.label: Primary school levelling-up programmes
sections.summary: In primary schools, levelling-up programmes are conducted in classes of eight to 10 and four to six.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the primary schools, levelling-up programmes, such as the Learning Support Programme for Lower Primary students and the School-based Dyslexia Remediation Programme for students with special education needs, are conducted in classes of eight to 10 and four to six respectively.

sections.label: OECD study on teacher duties
sections.summary: In the 2018 OECD study, teachers reported 3.8 hours a week on administrative duties, a drop of 1.5 hours from 2013.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the 2018 OECD study on secondary school teachers, we are happy to see some positive outcomes as our teachers have reported 3.8 hours a week spent on administrative duties, a drop of 1.5 hours compared to the 2013 survey.

sections.label: Recruiting more Allied Educators
sections.summary: Allied Educators would be most useful, so more are being recruited and resourced, especially for Learning Behavioural Support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Having an Allied Educator would be most useful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, indeed, we are looking into it – trying to recruit more Allied Educators and give more resourcing to support schools, especially through Allied Educators in what we call Learning Behavioural Support.

sections.label: Resources for pull-out classes
sections.summary: Additional resources are used for pull-out classes for Normal (Technical) and weaker students and lower primary Learning Support Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We are keeping the teachers in our system and we improve PTRs as a result.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And in general, what we wish to use the additional resources for are really pull-out classes – for Normal (Technical) and weaker students to give them more dedicated attention or in the lower primary, where we have the Learning Support Programme (LSP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We use these additional resources to be able to pull out the students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: That is why I am always worried about across-the-board fixing of class sizes because it can mean that all these additional resources today which are used to help weaker students, may disappear overnight.

sections.label: Administrative duties consent forms
sections.summary: The speaker describes administrative duties as consent forms being signed, collected, and attendance taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Regarding administrative duties, I am talking about consent forms, making sure they are signed, collecting them, and taking attendance.
